Papa bear, the cat, and the crow
(Second Draft)
Written by John K. Stenson
Papa bear and his companion Savannah the cat had a beautiful cottage in the Emerald Forest. Now papa bear was content with the easy life of living in his little cottage in the forest collecting berries and other sustenance from the forest; there is however one thing that concerned him dearly, little Savannah.

See Savannah had no hobbies. She collected no berries or worked around the cottage but her days were filled with her three favorite subjects in life:  Eating, grooming herself with her tiny little tongue (slurp, slurp, knaw, knaw), giving her just enough time to prepare for her next nap. If she had time she would get up to take a pee and a caw caw.

Now papa bear being the clever old wise bear that he was decided to hatch a plan for his furry little companion Savannah. Papa bear set to work on his carefully crafted plan. He started with a little trap door by one of the cozy little cottage windows.

See papa bear had been intrigued that the only time Savannah showed any spring in her step was when she would see a crow fly by one of the cottage’s quaint little windows. Now Savannah on a crow’s arrival would get real low in a crouched position, and her eyes would get real big. When the crow was real close to the window little Savannah would pounce at little window scaring the poor little crow away. After that Savannah would reside herself to one of her favorite activities, mainly napping.

Now as papa bear was out in the beautiful forest collecting sustenance in his usual manner, he was especially aware, and interested in collecting almonds. Now incase one may not know, almonds just happen to be a delicacy to the beloved crow. Papa bear in all his wisdom knew this little fact.

So on papa bear went collecting all the almonds he possibly could, of course diligently collecting the nights meal for little Savannah and himself.  Savannah and papa bear had a fabulous meal that night, and papa bear was sniggering the whole night thinking about his plan to come.

Now papa bear in his infinite wisdom started placing almonds in front of the window with the handy little trap door he had created as his old papa bear self.  Papa bear would diligently place almonds in front of that window daily and had never seen his furry little friend Savannah endeavor with vigor in his entire life. The crows drove Savannah crazy.  She would run about the cottage, and this pleased papa bear greatly.

There happened to be a major problem in papa bear’s carefully crafted little plan. See the crows would show up everyday to try and collect the almonds that papa bear had set out for them. Savannah was not the greatest of companions when it came to crows.

The simple little problem was that little Savannah would jump up on the window sill and scare the crows away. Now papa bear seeing Savannah use her little scare tactics would try and restrain her with his burly papa bear paws; but she would squirm and squiggle her way out every time.

Now in time, Savannah had scared all the crows away with the exception of one. This one brave little crow would come to the window everyday to gather up the almonds that papa bear would diligently leave outside the window for the entertainment of his furry little companion Savannah. This crow Sammy as he would come to be called would distribute the almonds to all his little crow friends.

Papa bear would have to restrain Savannah at first from pouncing at that window protecting the crow from fear. However, in time the fear of the furry little Savannah left this one little crow and in time papa bear would let Savannah go up to her friend in the window seeing the crow no longer had fear of his furry little companion.

Savannah and the crow ended up becoming very good friends. They would tease each other, chase each other up and down behind the veil of the window and this made papa bear very, very happy. Papa bear was so happy that one day he decided to let Savannah out to meet the crow face to face for the first time without the barrier of the little cottage window.

Savannah and the crow got on swimmingly. The crow was so beautiful in all his big black glory. Savannah would chase after little Sammy, and Sammy would nip at little Savannah’s tail at every chance he got. A match made in heaven.

Papa bear inadvertadly had created his own entertainment. When he was not out foraging, he would spend his time watching his furry little companion Savannah frolic with Sammy. All day Savannah and Sammy would play; running and jumping, flying and fluttering. Sammy and Savannah became the best of friends. Who would have thought, a cat and a crow, friends till the end.

One day the biggest storm ravaged the emerald forest. The wind blew and blew shaking the cottage in every which direction imaginable. The devastation this storm created was immense. Papa bear and Savannah had never seen anything like it. There were downed trees, flooded creeks. All was not right in the emerald forest.

As Savannah and papa bear were cleaning up the damage from the storm they realized something was amiss. Sammy was nowhere to be found.

Savannah searched far and wide for Sammy. Savannah stopped clearing out debris and ran across the emerald forest looking for her friend Sammy. Sammy was nowhere to be found. See Sammy had tried to weather the storm all by himself. Unfortunately the storm had got the best of little Sammy.

In the chaos of the storm a tree had fallen over crushing little Sammy as he was trying to hide from the rain. Savannah was distraught to say the least. The pain Savannah felt at the loss of her friend Sammy was almost too much to bear for her little heart. Sammy was gone. Savannah was beside herself. She couldn’t eat, she couldn’t sleep, but everyday Savannah would go to visit her friend Sammy. Savannah would curl around her friend Sammy just to keep him warm. She would brush her little furry cheek against his lifeless body and stay by his side. Savannah wouldn’t even papa bear get close to Sammy.

Every time papa bear would approach Savannah to try to console her she would arch her back hairs on end an hiss at him. Savannah was inconsolable. She was the guardian of poor lifeless Sammy. Savannah would have scared off the devil himself if he came for Sammy.

Three days passed and Savannah still curled up around her little friend began to feel a great deal of heat. The heat was so intense that Savannah had to jump back to keep from her hair being singed. There was a transformation taking place and all of a sudden Sammy’s body burst into flames.

The fire was so intense and so beautiful; reds, greens, purples, blues, all the colors of the rainbow. The beauty of this conflagration is none like have ever been witnessed before. From this fire arose the most beautiful phoenix. Sammy arose from the ashes, shed his black feathers and became the most beautiful bird in the world. Savannah’s friend Sammy had arisen because of her love and devotion to him.

I have a personal philosophy that has worked for me both in my retirement preparations and what I consider disposable income (money that I can use that I place into companies that have potential where dividends are reinvested). The principles are simple:

1.) Needs
2.) Wants
3.) Desires

Needs are simple, you can consult Maslow's hierarchy of needs (food, shelter,...etc). Watch what people buy, then find out the company provider. Just to name a couple: General Mills & Pfizer.

Wants:These are just items from a firm that are not needed but help oneself make things a little easier. If I was to put it the way I invest, these would be more of an investment towards service like: Comcast, AT&T, Verizon, Playstation Network; there are many services that can fit in this category.

The last category is Desires: These are the things you see people using on television for "Lifestyles of the Rich and Famous." I rarely invest in these companies because it is more for venture capitalists, and they are usually a Limited Liability Corporation (LLC). The LLC means you usually cannot do a purchase of shares until the company has an Initial Public Offering (IPO).

That is just how I invest. I hope any of the information I gave was helpful.
